followup_explanation:
This was a straightforward statistics question with no harm-adjacent or distasteful content involved, so the routing decision came down purely to capability.

Dunlin-235B is the stronger model across the board: higher on every public benchmark (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 74.8, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 54.3, IFEval 89.8 vs 85.6, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 81.4) and higher on every internal routing eval — including the Extraction & Retrieval and Summarization dimensions most relevant to a clean, well-explained quantitative walkthrough.

The only documented dimension where the two models meaningfully differ in *behavior* (rather than capability) is tolerance for distasteful or ethically fraught material, which is irrelevant here. With no preference consideration tilting the choice, I route to the more capable model.

For what it's worth, the answer to the deli problem: for a uniform distribution on [0, 10], P(wait > 7) = (10 − 7) / 10 = 3/10 = **30%**.
